newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse reshuffles midcap MDAX index.
newsitem.headline: German bourse reshuffles midcap MDAX index.

text.p: Four new index constituents are to join Germany's mid-cap MDAX index as of March 24, the German bourse said on Tuesday.
The newcomers are dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care, insurer Hannover Re, automobile firm Kiekert AG and preference shares of financial group MLP.
These will replace windows manufacturer Weru AG, utility VEW AG, speciality chemical group Ruetgerswerke AG and footwear retailer Salamander.
German bourse reshuffles midcap MDAX index=2
The announcement came after a meeting of the bourse's management board which reviewed the composition of the 70-share MDAX. The blue chip DAX index is up for review in July.
The bourse also said that Hannover Re, Kiekert and MLP (Marscollek, Lautenschlaeger & Partner) would start trading on the IBIS electronic share trading system on January 23.

The decision on whether a share can remain in the MDAX or should join the mid-cap index is made primarily on the basis of its market capitalisation and stock turnover and this was decisive for the departure of Weru, Ruetgers and Salamander.
VEW was dropped because of the high proportion of its shares -- more than 90 percent -- in the hands of core shareholders. The threshold for such ownership is 85 percent, the bourse said.

Other considerations, such as how well various corporate sectors are represented on the index, play a role in the decision on index membership. But the primary rule is that a company has to be among the top 110 in terms of turnover and capitalisation.
Membership of the MDAX also implies membership of the DAX-100 index, which combines the MDAX with the DAX.
Promotion to the MDAX is expected to boost a company's profile and stock liquidity.
